posts.cooked:
For this question, I feel none of the given answers are correct.

Option 1 seems the closest, but it can also fail when both ERROR and WARNING are in the same line. The -o option should be used along with the grep command to get the output.

Is this a valid concern? Please do correct me if I’m wrong.

Thanks!

posts.name: Archismaan Pal
posts.cooked:
The server.log file is a log file so it is common knowledge that each line will either contain warning or error not both.

Also last option has -w which solves your some-line-might-have-both issue.

Hope this helps…

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
MusicViking:

Option 1 seems the closest, but it can also fail when both ERROR and WARNING are in the same line.

Correct.

23f2001159:

The server.log file is a log file so it is common knowledge that each line will either contain warning or error not both.

Correct.

MusicViking:

The -o option should be used along with the grep command to get the output.

Correct, if you are worried about the case of a line having both error and warning, you should do

grep -Eo `ERROR|WARNING` | wc -l

instead.

MusicViking:

Is this a valid concern?

Yes! Glad you are thinking outside the box and considering these edge cases as well.

23f2001159:

Also last option has -w which solves your some-line-might-have-both issue.

This is not true, last option runs on grep -E, not on grep -Eo, hence it will count number of words in the entire line of the log.
